To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the muted (mu, also called HPS-3) gene, a mouse model for Hermanssky-Pudlak syndrome in humans, encodes a novel 185 amino acid polypeptide, which regulates the synthesis and/or function of highly specialized sub cellular organelles such a melanosomes, lysosomes and platelet dense bodies.

the muted gene defines a novel ubiquitiously expressed transcript, specifying an 185 amino acid predicted protein, that is a component of vesicles and regulates vesicle trafficking in mammalian cells, and that the muted gene is present only among mammals.
the gene encoding the muted protein has been cloned and that it regulates the synthesis of vesicles in the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of Hermansky-Putlak syndrome (HPS).
the elucidation of the molecular basis of a human disease, HPS.
the identification and characterization of the gene responsible for a human disease and the elucidation of its function in the regulation of vesicle trafficking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mu gene is essential for the synthesis and function of highly specialized sub cellular organelles.
the muted gene is a member in the novel gene set of the higher eukaryotic genomes which regulates the synthesis of melanosomes, otoliths and platelet dense bodies.
the mu gene encodes a novel protein that regulates the trafficking of vesicles containing specialized organelles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muted (mu ) gene defines a novel protein that controls vesicle trafficking and is required for the synthesis of specialized organelles.
the muted gene is a novel gene, whose protein product regulates vesicle trafficking, and whose expression is lost in the mu allele of the muted mouse, a model of Hermansky-Pdudlak syndrome in humans.
the gene for the muted mouse defines a novel protein regulating vesicle trafficking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the muted gene defines a novel family of proteins which regulate vesicle trafficking.
the mu gene is required for the formation of melanosomes, otoliths, and platelet dense bodies.
the muted gene is the first of a new gene class which regulates the trafficking of vesicles within melanocytes, platelets, and other cells.
